summary: Shoson Miyamoto was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo (~1928–1954) and later as professor at Komazawa University (~1954–1968).
Shou-chien Shih is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He served as a professor at National Taiwan University (~1990–2003) and was director of the National Palace Museum (~2004–2006).

Shoyu Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1957). He served as a professor at Musashino University (~1970–1995) and chairperson of Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai (1982–1995).

Shozen Kumoi studied at Otani University (~1938–1941) and worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as an assistant professor at Otani University (1948–1981) and later as a professor at Bukkyo University (1982).
Shri Krishna Saksena is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held positions as professor at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaii.

Shridhar Ramkrishna Bhandarkar was an Indology scholar. He served as assistant to the professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1884), professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College (~1884–1909), and permanent professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai (~1909–1916).

Shrikant S. Bahulkar studied Indology and Buddhist studies under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale. He has held posts at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth and served as chief editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak (~1902–1906). He served as professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1927) and general secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference (~1920–1943).
Shrivatsa Goswami is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1968–1974) and held a post at the Vrindaban Research Institute.

Shu-chen Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia (~2000–2007) under Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen C. Lang. She also served there as a teaching assistant in 1996.

Shu-fen Chen studied linguistics and Indology at National Tsing Hua University, completing doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock (~1995–2000). She was appointed professor at National Tsing Hua University (~2000).
Shu-fen Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, history, and archaeology. She has held posts at Academia Sinica and as a professor at its Institute of History and Philology.
Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who held posts at Karnatak University as a professor and at the University of Mysore in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits.
Shudo Ishii, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned a BA from Komazawa University (~1962–1966) under Shigeo Kamata. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1974–2014).
Shudo Iwai completed doctoral coursework in Buddhist studies at Komazawa University (~1967–1973) and served as a professor there.
Shuen-fu Lin is a Sinologist who earned his PhD from Princeton University (~1968–1972). He served as professor of Chinese language and literature at the University of Michigan (~1973–2012).

Shuhong Chang was a scholar in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University (~1918–1923) and Zhejiang University. He served as director of the Dunhuang Academy (~1944–1982).
Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at Ryukoku University, Bukkyo University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and Musashino University.

Shujun Motegi studied Indology and philosophy under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi at Banaras Hindu University (1973–1975) and earned an MA at Kyoto University (~1975–1977). He served as professor of ethics at Shinshu University.

Shuken Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed graduate studies at Komazawa University (~1970–1973), where he served as a research assistant (~1973–1977). He later held a post at Aichi Gakuin University.
